newsitem.title: CHINA: Taiwan-invested bank buys office in Shanghai zone.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan-invested bank buys office in Shanghai zone.

text.p: A Taiwan-invested bank has signed a contract to buy an 1,800-sq-m (19,375-sq-ft) office in Shanghai's premier development zone, the Pudong New Area, the Xinmin Evening News said.
The First Sino Bank is China's first joint venture bank between China and Taiwanese business interests, the newspaper's late Saturday edition said.
It gave no further details, but Chinese media have reported that the bank was set up in January 1997 with the Shanghai Pudong Development Bank and registered capital of $100 million.
The Taiwan partners have not been identified in China's official press, other than to say they are a group of Taiwanese businessmen registered overseas, some in the United States.
The joint venture was expected to apply for permission to handle domestic yuan currency business, and only banks based in Pudong are permitted to conduct yuan currency business.
The official Shanghai-based Business News reported in January that Taiwan-invested firms would be the bank's main clients, followed by firms with investment from overseas Chinese.
Shanghai has designated Pudong, across the Huangpu River from the city's famous waterfront Bund, as a future regional financial centre, and is using administrative means to speed its development.
Foreign banks in Shanghai wishing to do local currency business have been told they must move their offices away from central Shanghai into Pudong.
Earlier this month, Citibank became the first foreign bank to move across the river.
Shanghai also plans to move all its exchanges to Pudong.

The Shanghai Real Estate Exchange Centre opened for business there last Friday, the same day work began on the building that will house the Shanghai Commodity Exchange, which plans to move to the area later in 1997, local press has reported.

The Shanghai Cereals and Oils Exchange has already moved to Pudong, and the Shanghai Stock Exchange will also move later this year, followed by other major markets before the end of the century, the local press has said.

A number of city government departments including the Shanghai Housing and Land Management Committee, the Shanghai Foreign Trade Commission and Shanghai Foreign Investment Commission will also shortly move to Pudong. ((-- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004))
